selection_basis: The first four actionable records emitted by the canonical review queue after claim cleanup batch seven completed and before any batch-eight rewrite was applied.

observed_initial_queue.blocked_reason: The higher-priority preview consisted of sensitive or restricted records requiring actual-source and safety review rather than automatic practical rewriting.

guardrail: This batch preserves only low-risk operational or logical procedures. It removes inherited unsupported quantitative, first-party, mechanism and performance claims, adds no source and promotes no entry to reviewed.

entries.decision: Remove unsupported claims about repetition, judgment improvement and training targets, fabricated source-tracing outcomes, rigid timing rules and health, money or civic examples. Preserve a source-lineage procedure: trace repeated claims to the material they rely on, note shared documents, datasets or organizations, and avoid counting repeated summaries as independent support.

Remove fabricated calibration statistics, effect claims, fixed probability increments, action thresholds, reminder schedules and first-party examples. Preserve a qualitative judgment log: state the current confidence level, record the main support and uncertainty, name one observable fact that would change the judgment, and compare the prediction with what later happened.

Remove unsupported historical and cognitive claims, fabricated volunteer and cohort outcomes, fixed daily habit targets, emotional mechanism claims, political and health examples and arbitrary numerical decision thresholds. Preserve a narrow decision preflight: state the assumption, name one observation that would weaken it, check that condition before committing, and update or escalate when it is found.

Remove fabricated pause experiments, cognitive-mechanism claims, probability training bins, daily quotas and high-stakes hiring or health examples. Preserve the underlying logical check: split a compound statement into A and B, compare A with A-and-B, and remember that every case satisfying both conditions is already included among the cases satisfying A.
